text.title: RAG Policy Thresholds: Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes when running a RAG policy with numeric thresholds in real teams. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Watermelon reporting: one signal is over its `red_threshold`, but the published project colour is Green or Amber because signals were averaged or the PM relabelled the result.
failure-mode.detector: Published colour is better than the worst computed signal colour and `review_log` contains no override entry for that cycle; or the compute step contains any averaging / weighting of signals.
failure-mode.repair: Recompute as worst-signal-wins (`r-worst-signal-wins`). Re-issue the report with the computed colour; if an override was justified, add the `review_log` entry with reason and person, remembering that Red cannot be overridden down (`r-override-logged-never-downgrades-red`).

failure-mode.description: Prose threshold: a signal row says "significant", "material" or "trending badly" instead of a number, so the colour is renegotiated every week.
failure-mode.detector: Any `amber_threshold` or `red_threshold` that is not a number, or a comparator missing; validator rejects, or the same signal value produced different colours in two cycles.
failure-mode.repair: Replace with a numeric threshold and comparator tied to an evidence anchor (`r-threshold-numeric-with-comparator`). If no number can be agreed, delete the signal rather than keep a judgement slot.

failure-mode.description: Collapsed Amber band: amber and red thresholds are equal, or swapped for a `lt` signal, so the project jumps from Green straight to Red with no warning window.
failure-mode.detector: For `gt`/`gte`: `red_threshold <= amber_threshold`. For `lt`/`lte`: `red_threshold >= amber_threshold`. Or colour history shows Green followed directly by Red for the same signal across many cycles.
failure-mode.repair: Fix the ordering so red lies strictly beyond amber in the comparator's direction (`r-red-strictly-beyond-amber`); check every `lt` signal copied from the default `gt` rows in the skeleton.

failure-mode.description: Opinion as input: `input_source` is "PM estimate" or "team check-in", so the number fed to a precise threshold is itself a gut call.
failure-mode.detector: `input_source` does not name a system plus a repeatable query/export; two people asked for the value on the same day produce different numbers.
failure-mode.repair: Point the signal at a named query (JQL filter, Sentry saved search, finance export) and express schedule/budget as percent variance against plan (`r-input-source-is-a-query`). Until then the signal is excluded from the compute.

failure-mode.description: Red without consequence: the compute says Red, `actions.red` says "discuss at next sync", and the project stays Red for weeks with no escalation.
failure-mode.detector: `actions.red` lacks a named playbook or a time bound; or colour history shows Red in two or more consecutive cycles with no escalation record.
failure-mode.repair: Rewrite `actions.red` with a named escalation path and a deadline for the first step, fired at compute time (`r-red-action-named-and-time-bound`). Backfill the escalation for any currently-Red project the same day.

failure-mode.description: Fossil thresholds: the policy has not been reviewed in over 90 days; some signals never fire, others fire every week and are ignored, and the last incident was not predicted by any of them.
failure-mode.detector: `header.last_reviewed` older than 90 days; a signal with zero Amber/Red in two review periods; or a post-mortem in the period with no matching signal in the policy.
failure-mode.repair: Run the quarterly review before the next compute: prune dead signals, add a signal per unflagged incident with an evidence anchor, bump version and `last_reviewed` (`r-review-within-90-days-prunes-and-adds`, `r-evidence-anchor-per-signal`).
